checks.evidence: ProjectLibrary.swift lines 36, 39 and 65 require schemaVersion == 1 when validated() runs. ProjectLibraryTests.swift lines 400–410 decode a schemaVersion 2 snapshot and expect subsequent validation to throw.

ProjectLibrary.swift line 67 compares Set(projects.map(\.id)).count to projects.count, including archived projects. ProjectLibraryTests.swift lines 412–417 duplicate a serialized project and expect duplicateID from validated().

activeProject at line 48 matches activeID and requires !isArchived; validated() line 68 rejects nil. The focused metadata test covers a nonexistent activeID. An explicitly archived activeID is not covered in this test file's serialized metadata cases.

validated() line 66 rejects zero or more than 64 array entries. All entries, including archived projects, contribute. Serialized empty-array rejection is covered; the 64-project test exercises mutation capacity, not serialized 65-entry validation.

normalizedName at lines 50–61 trims whitespace/newlines, then requires 1–80 Swift Characters and rejects remaining control/newline scalars except U+200C/U+200D. validated() line 71 applies this to every project. Existing name tests cover invalid mutation inputs; they do not exercise invalid names injected into serialized records.

ProjectLibrary uses synthesized Codable and a distinct validated() stage. ProjectLibraryTests explicitly expects syntactically valid but semantically invalid metadata to decode before validated() throws. SceneCodec.swift likewise decodes LightingScene then calls validated(). Direct JSONDecoder.decode alone is not established as the validation boundary.

A serialized name such as "\nPortrait\n" would be trimmed to "Portrait" by validated(), and its length is checked after trimming. The inspected contract requires malformed/oversized-data handling and no data loss; ARCHITECTURE says "No silent overwrite on decode failure." Neither explicitly prohibits successful display-name normalization. ProjectLibraryTests lines 12–32 expect constructor name normalization, and lines 36–53 expect legacy scene schema migration while preserving legacy bytes. Therefore padded-name normalization is not classified as a must-fix.

No repair of schemaVersion, duplicate project IDs, empty/excessive count, or invalid active identity occurs in validated(). Malformed JSON goes through JSONDecoder without fallback at the observed decode call sites. Tests lines 56–77 assert corrupt legacy/library data produces errors and retains bytes; those tests were not executed.
